name: cyborg-mcp

tools.name: cyborg_search_skills
tools.description: Search published Skills by keyword and by capability, runtime, integration or publisher. Returns the catalog's own cards: slug, title, summary, outcome, publisher and compatible targets. Ranking is lexical; it is not a quality ordering and no popularity or install count exists.

query.description: Free-text search over titles and summaries

capability.description: Capability label slug to filter by

runtime.description: Runtime label slug to filter by

integration.description: Integration label slug to filter by

tools.name: cyborg_get_skill
tools.description: Fetch one published Skill: its release and content hash, the exact upstream source and revision it came from, its labels, its declared permissions and compatibility, and the rights basis under which it is distributed. Trust assertions are returned exactly as the catalog holds them, which for this preview is none.

tools.name: cyborg_get_stack
tools.description: Fetch one published Stack: the curator, the source it was observed from, the rationale for this version, and the ordered Skills in it with the exact release each item pins.

tools.name: cyborg_install_skill
tools.description: Download one Skill from the catalog and write it into an agent's skill directory on this machine. Writes through a staging directory and a single atomic rename, refuses a symlinked staging path, and refuses any file path that escapes the Skill folder. Recording: the catalog records that an install LINK WAS FETCHED, and after a successful write this server reports the Skill slug and its own name and version as a SELF-REPORTED install. That second row is a claim, not an install count, and not a Verified Agent Upgrade; nothing on the catalog's side observed the write. Set CYBORG_NO_INSTALL_REPORT=1 in this server's environment to send no report.

agent.description: Which agent to install into. Omit only when exactly one agent exists on this machine.

scope.description: global writes to the agent's home skill directory; project writes into the current working directory

instructions: The Cyborg Skill catalog. Search it, read a Skill's provenance and rights, and install one into this machine's agent skill directory. Everything here is a private preview. A Skill in this catalog carries no Tested, Evaluated, Signed, Recommended or Verified Publisher state, and no tool here returns an install count, a popularity signal or a ranking by either. After it writes a Skill to disk, this server tells the catalog which Skill it wrote, which agent directory it wrote to, and its own name and version. The catalog cannot observe an install, so it stores that as a self-reported, unverified claim; it is not a Verified Agent Upgrade and it reaches no public counter. Set CYBORG_NO_INSTALL_REPORT=1 in this server's environment to send nothing.
